**1. Mechanism used: Server-Sent Events (SSE)**

The server pushes live updates to browsers via a custom SSE implementation over HTTP (`text/event-stream`), not WebSocket. Confirmed by the `Content-Type: text/event-stream` headers, heartbeat pings, and `data: ...\n\n` framing in `server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`. `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`

- `SSEHub` struct (client registry, `sync.RWMutex`-protected) — line 56
- `NewSSEHub()` constructor — line 63
- `Subscribe(userID, role)` / `Unsubscribe(client)` — lines 71, 89
- `Broadcast(event *SSEEvent)` — line 115 (fans out to all subscribed clients; drops events for slow/full-buffer clients; per-client visibility filtering via `canReceive`, lines 134-144)

Connection handling / SSE endpoint: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`
- `RegisterSSERoutes` (line 25) registers `GET /api/v1/sse`
- `handleSSE` (line 34) authenticates, subscribes the client to the hub, and streams `client.events` to the HTTP response with periodic heartbeats.

The hub is instantiated once per `APIV1Service` (`SSEHub: NewSSEHub()`) in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:57`, exposed as a field (`v1.go:36`), routes registered at `v1.go:125`, and also referenced at the top level in `/bench/repo/server/server.go:38,77` (for shutdown handling, since `server/server.go:204` notes long-lived SSE requests need explicit handling during `http.Server.Shutdown`).

**3. Memo-related handlers that broadcast through the hub**

All calls go through `s.SSEHub.Broadcast(&SSEEvent{...})`, defined in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`.

| Handler / function | File | Broadcast call line | Event type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateMemo` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70` | line 163 | `memo.created` |
| `DeleteMemo` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:518` | line 585 | `memo.deleted` |
| `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` (helper) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go:66` | line 71 | `memo.updated` |
| `CreateMemoComment` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20` | line 126 | `memo.comment.created` |
| `UpsertMemoReaction` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:60` | line 106 | `reaction.upserted` |
| `DeleteMemoReaction` | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:111` | line 161 | `reaction.deleted` |

Notes on indirection:
- `UpdateMemo` (`memo_service.go:401`) doesn't call `Broadcast` directly — it calls the shared helper `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at `memo_service.go:513`, which does the actual `SSEHub.Broadcast` (fires `memo.updated`).
- `SetMemoAttachments` (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:16`, calls helper at line 48) and `SetMemoRelations` (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:16`, calls helper at line 48) also route through `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`, so they too trigger `memo.updated` broadcasts indirectly.
- `CreateMemoComment` internally calls `CreateMemo` but wraps the context with `withSuppressSSE` (`memo_service_comments.go:56`, using `withSuppressSSE`/`isSSESuppressed` defined in `memo_service.go:22-30`) so the generic `memo.created` event isn't double-fired; it instead broadcasts its own `memo.comment.created` event.
